findings.title: Status check uses 'succeeded' but AiJobApplicationSummaryStatus only has 'none' | 'current' | 'regenerating'
findings.detail: Line 26: `summaryStatus === "succeeded"` will never be true. The AiJobApplicationSummaryStatus model (app/models/ai_job_application_summary_status.rb) defines enum values `none: 0, current: 1, regenerating: 2`. The frontend type (jobApplication.ts line 4) correctly defines `"none" | "current" | "regenerating"`. But JobApplicationNavItem still checks for the old AiJobApplicationSummary.status value 'succeeded' instead of the new 'current'. The Harvey ball fit indicator in the sidebar nav list will never render.
findings.fix: Change line 26 from `summaryStatus === "succeeded"` to `summaryStatus === "current"`. Also consider adding `summaryStatus === "regenerating"` if the score should display during regeneration.

findings.title: ai_summary_status_change handler does not invalidate jobApplicationsForStage
findings.detail: The new ai_summary_status_change case invalidates ['jobApplication'] and ['aiJobApplicationSummary'] but not 'jobApplicationsForStage'. JobApplicationListContainer (line 222-223) passes aiJobApplicationSummaryStatus.status and scorePercentage to JobApplicationNavItem via data from useInfiniteJobApplicationsForStage. When a summary reaches 'current' status via this websocket event, the list view sidebar items will not update until the user navigates away and back. The GlobalChannelHandler's AI_SUMMARY_COMPLETE event does invalidate jobApplicationsForStage (line 251), so this only matters if: (a) the JobChannel event fires without a corresponding GlobalChannel event, or (b) the JobChannel event fires first and the user needs immediate feedback. Given that both events exist for the same completion lifecycle, this is not a blocker but a potential race/gap.
findings.fix: Add `queryClient.invalidateQueries("jobApplicationsForStage");` to the ai_summary_status_change case, matching the pattern in WebsocketGlobalChannelHandler's AI_SUMMARY_COMPLETE handler.

findings.title: ai_summary_status_change handler does not use payload.jobApplicationId for targeted invalidation
findings.detail: The handler invalidates all ['jobApplication'] queries (every cached job application) instead of targeting just the affected one. Comparing with WebsocketGlobalChannelHandler line 153 (attachExternalResumeComplete) which does `queryCache.invalidateQueries(["jobApplication", Number(data.payload.jobApplicationId)])` for a targeted invalidation. The backend broadcasts `payload: { jobApplicationId: job_application.id }` per the spec, so the data is available. The broad invalidation works correctly but causes unnecessary refetches for all cached job applications. This is consistent with the AI_SUMMARY_COMPLETE handler in GlobalChannelHandler (line 225) which also does a broad invalidation, so this follows the existing pattern.
findings.fix: No change needed for consistency with existing patterns. Could be optimized later to `queryClient.invalidateQueries(["jobApplication", data.payload.jobApplicationId])` if performance is a concern.

findings.title: useCallback dependency array does not include setActiveJobApplicationId
findings.detail: handleJobMessage uses setActiveJobApplicationId (line 71) but it is not in the dependency array (line 83). This is technically a missing dependency. However, setActiveJobApplicationId comes from React.useState which produces a stable setter, so this will not cause bugs in practice. Pre-existing issue, not introduced by this change.
findings.fix: No fix needed -- React.useState setters are referentially stable.

findings.title: AiJobApplicationSummary type is still exported and used by consumers
findings.detail: The AiJobApplicationSummary and AiJobApplicationSummaryFull interfaces remain exported and are actively consumed by: (1) useAiJobApplicationSummary.ts query hook, (2) PlatoTab.tsx via the hook's return data. No consumer imports AiJobApplicationSummary from this file directly by type name -- the types are inferred through the hook's return type. The type definitions appear correct and consistent with the full summary endpoint's response shape. No issues found.

findings.title: AiJobApplicationSummaryStatus type matches backend model and serializer
findings.detail: Verified the type definition against: (1) AiJobApplicationSummaryStatus model enum (none/current/regenerating), (2) AiJobApplicationSummaryStatusSerializer attributes (id, ai_job_application_summary_id, status, score_percentage, headline, integrated_role_analysis, updated_at). All fields match after camelCase conversion. The type correctly allows null for aiJobApplicationSummaryStatus on the JobApplication interface (line 21), handling the case where no status record exists.

findings.title: No payload validation on ai_summary_status_change, but matches existing patterns
findings.detail: The ai_summary_status_change handler does not validate data.payload or its shape. However, this is consistent with all other cases in the same handler -- wwr_listing_published/updated (lines 55-59) do not validate payload either, and docx_to_pdf_conversion_complete (line 71) accesses data.payload.jobApplicationId without a guard. The handler's outer guard `if (data.event != null)` is the only validation, matching every other case. No security concern since this is an authenticated ActionCable channel.
findings.fix: No fix needed -- consistent with existing patterns.

summary: One BLOCKER found: JobApplicationNavItem checks summaryStatus === 'succeeded' but the new AiJobApplicationSummaryStatus type only contains 'none' | 'current' | 'regenerating'. The fit indicator Harvey ball in the sidebar list will never render. One MED: the ai_summary_status_change websocket handler does not invalidate jobApplicationsForStage, meaning the list view sidebar may not update when a summary completes via this event path. The WebsocketJobChannelHandler's new case otherwise follows existing patterns correctly -- same invalidation style, same lack of payload validation, same dependency array conventions.
